The problem: greedy sequence where $a_{n+1}$ is the smallest integer greater than $a_n$ sharing a common factor with all earlier terms. Prove the sequence is eventually (indeed globally) periodic in the sense $a_{n+T} = a_n + L$.

The rubric requires:
- (C) characterization: an integer $m \ge a_1$ is a term iff its prime support meets the prime support of every term (equivalently every earlier term).
- (F) finiteness / large-prime erasure lemma: membership depends only on primes in a finite set, proved for ALL terms.
- (P) periodicity assembly: $L$ = product of relevant primes, membership invariant under $m \to m+L$ for every $m \ge a_1$, $T$ = number of terms in a window of length $L$, giving $a_{n+T} = a_n + L$ for all $n \ge 1$.
